questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A homeowner's property is valued at $400,000 and has an outstanding mortgage balance of $250,000. The owner's equity is:

explanations.a: $650,000 is the sum of value and debt, not the difference.
explanations.b: $250,000 is the outstanding loan balance, not the owner's equity.
explanations.c: Equity equals the property's market value minus all liens: $400,000 − $250,000 = $150,000.
explanations.d: $400,000 is the property's full market value, not the owner's net equity.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A buyer purchases a home for $320,000 and makes a $64,000 down payment. The loan-to-value (LTV) ratio at origination is:

explanations.a: 20% is the down payment percentage, not the LTV.
explanations.c: 64% has no direct relationship to the numbers in this transaction.
explanations.d: 25% is neither the LTV nor the down payment percentage in this scenario.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: Compared to a 15-year fixed-rate mortgage for the same loan amount and interest rate, a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage will generally have:

answers.text: lower monthly payments but higher total interest paid over the life of the loan
higher monthly payments and lower total interest paid over the life of the loan
the same monthly payments because the interest rate is identical
lower monthly payments and lower total interest paid over the life of the loan

explanations.a: Spreading principal repayment over 30 years lowers each payment, but the balance accrues interest for twice as long, resulting in far more total interest paid.
explanations.b: The 30-year loan has lower, not higher, monthly payments; the 15-year loan pays off faster with less total interest.
explanations.c: The same rate does not mean the same payment; the 30-year loan has a lower payment because it amortizes over more months.
explanations.d: Lower payments do not mean lower total interest; the longer term means more months of interest accumulation.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: In the early years of a fully amortized fixed-rate mortgage, the majority of each monthly payment is applied to:

answers.text: reduction of the outstanding loan principal
insurance escrow and property tax reserves
prepayment of future principal installments
interest, with only a small portion reducing the principal balance

explanations.a: In early amortization, most of the payment services interest; principal reduction is a small share until later in the loan.
explanations.b: Escrow for taxes and insurance is a separate payment component from principal and interest.
explanations.c: Prepayment of future principal is not how standard amortization works; each payment is allocated per the current balance.
explanations.d: Because interest is calculated on the full outstanding balance in early years, most of the payment covers interest and very little goes to principal.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: The principal and interest (P&I) portion of a mortgage payment consists of:

answers.text: the loan balance and the lender's origination fee
repayment of the loan balance and compensation to the lender for the use of borrowed funds
the down payment and the mortgage insurance premium
escrow deposits for taxes and the loan servicer's monthly fee

explanations.a: Origination fees are paid at closing, not as part of the ongoing monthly P&I payment.
explanations.b: P&I covers the reduction of the principal balance (repayment of the borrowed amount) and interest (the cost of borrowing the remaining balance).
explanations.c: The down payment is made at closing and mortgage insurance is a separate component of the total payment, neither constitutes P&I.
explanations.d: Tax and insurance escrow payments are separate from the P&I component.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: As a fully amortized mortgage matures over time, the portion of each monthly payment applied to principal:

answers.text: decreases because the lender's risk increases as the loan ages
remains constant because the payment amount is fixed throughout the term
increases as the outstanding balance falls and less interest is owed each month
is set permanently by the lender at origination and never changes

explanations.a: Lender risk generally decreases as the loan is paid down; and it does not affect how the fixed payment is allocated.
explanations.b: Although the total payment is fixed, the split between principal and interest shifts with each payment.
explanations.c: Interest is calculated on the declining balance, so as the balance falls, less interest is owed and more of the fixed payment reduces principal.
explanations.d: The allocation between principal and interest changes with each payment based on the current outstanding balance.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A borrower pays two discount points to obtain a lower interest rate on a $300,000 mortgage. How much does the borrower pay at closing for the points?

explanations.a: One point equals 1% of the loan amount. Two points = 2% × $300,000 = $6,000.
explanations.b: $600 would be 0.2% of the loan, which does not correspond to two points.
explanations.c: $3,000 equals one point (1%), not two points.
explanations.d: $60,000 would be 20% of the loan amount, far more than two points.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: An investor purchases a rental property for $200,000, receives $18,000 in net operating income during the first year, and sells the property after one year for $210,000. The investor's approximate total return on the initial investment is:

explanations.a: 9% represents only the income return ($18,000 ÷ $200,000) and ignores the $10,000 capital gain.
explanations.b: 5% represents only the appreciation ($10,000 ÷ $200,000) and ignores the income.
explanations.c: 4.5% does not correspond to either component or the total.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A fully amortized loan is one in which:

answers.text: the entire balance is due in a single lump-sum balloon payment at the end of the term
equal periodic payments over the loan term retire both principal and interest so the balance reaches zero at maturity
only interest is remitted each month and the principal balance never declines
the interest rate adjusts periodically based on a published financial index

explanations.a: A balloon payment loan has a large lump-sum due at the end; a fully amortized loan reaches a zero balance through regular payments.
explanations.b: Full amortization means each payment reduces the outstanding balance, and the final payment retires the loan completely.
explanations.c: An interest-only loan leaves the principal balance intact; full amortization reduces it to zero.
explanations.d: Adjustable-rate mortgages change rates over time; that feature is separate from whether the loan is amortizing.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: An interest-only mortgage differs from a fully amortizing mortgage in that an interest-only loan:

answers.text: carries a lower interest rate because no principal is ever repaid
gives the lender a partial ownership interest until the principal is repaid
leaves the full original principal balance outstanding at the end of the interest-only period
requires a larger down payment than a conventional amortizing mortgage

explanations.a: Interest-only loans do not automatically carry lower rates; the borrower still pays interest and the rate reflects credit risk.
explanations.b: A lender does not obtain ownership interest through an interest-only loan; the lender holds a lien.
explanations.c: Because no principal is being repaid during the interest-only period, the entire original loan amount remains outstanding when that period ends.
explanations.d: Down payment requirements are not necessarily higher for interest-only loans; they depend on lender guidelines.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: An adjustable-rate mortgage with a 2/1/5 cap structure means the interest rate:

answers.text: can rise no more than 2% at the first adjustment, 1% at each subsequent periodic adjustment, and 5% total over the life of the loan
adjusts every two years, has a 1% floor, and cannot exceed 5% per year
has a two-year fixed period, resets once, and the lifetime cap is 5% above the start rate
may increase 2% per year in the first period, then 1% per year up to a 5% maximum above the initial rate

explanations.a: A 2/1/5 cap means: first-adjustment cap of 2%, periodic (subsequent) adjustment cap of 1%, and lifetime cap of 5% above the initial rate.
explanations.b: The numbers in a 2/1/5 cap refer to adjustment limits, not adjustment frequency or a floor rate.
explanations.c: The 2 in the cap refers to the first adjustment limit, not a fixed period; all three numbers refer to rate change limits.
explanations.d: The periodic cap of 1% applies to each subsequent adjustment, not a rising annual schedule.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A construction loan differs from a permanent mortgage in that a construction loan typically:

answers.text: fully amortizes from the first payment and carries a 30-year term
is originated at a below-market rate subsidized by the federal government
is guaranteed by the FHA for all residential construction projects
is a short-term loan that is replaced by permanent take-out financing when construction is complete

explanations.a: Construction loans are short-term, typically one to two years; they do not amortize over a 30-year period.
explanations.b: Construction loans are not automatically subsidized; they typically carry higher rates than permanent mortgages due to risk.
explanations.c: FHA has specific construction programs, but not all residential construction loans are FHA-guaranteed.
explanations.d: A construction loan funds the building phase and is paid off and replaced by a longer-term permanent mortgage when the project is complete.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A home equity line of credit (HELOC) allows a homeowner to:

answers.text: obtain title insurance against equity-based claims from creditors
borrow against the equity in the home, typically secured by a subordinate lien on the property
sell a portion of the home's equity to an investor without any repayment obligation
receive a lump sum from the lender in exchange for a share of the home's future appreciation

explanations.a: Title insurance protects against ownership claims, not equity-related borrowing.
explanations.b: A HELOC is a revolving credit facility that uses the homeowner's equity as collateral, secured by a mortgage or deed of trust lien on the property.
explanations.c: Selling equity without repayment describes an equity-sharing arrangement, not a HELOC.
explanations.d: Sharing future appreciation without a repayment obligation describes a shared equity or reverse mortgage product, not a HELOC.

questions.name: Finance
questions.keyword: FHA lower down payment mortgage insurance
questions.text: An FHA-insured mortgage loan differs from a conventional loan in that an FHA loan:

answers.text: requires a 20% down payment to avoid a funding fee
is funded and originated directly by the federal government
allows a lower down payment and more flexible credit standards but requires mortgage insurance premiums
is available exclusively to first-time homebuyers purchasing primary residences

explanations.a: FHA allows down payments as low as 3.5%; the 20% threshold is associated with avoiding private mortgage insurance on conventional loans.
explanations.b: FHA loans are made by private, FHA-approved lenders; the federal government insures them, not originates them.
explanations.c: FHA-insured loans permit lower down payments and more lenient credit qualifications in exchange for mandatory mortgage insurance premiums (MIP) that protect the lender.
explanations.d: FHA loans are not limited to first-time buyers; repeat buyers and non-owner occupants may also qualify under certain conditions.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A conventional mortgage loan is one that:

answers.text: is not insured or guaranteed by a federal government agency
is guaranteed by the Department of Veterans Affairs for eligible veterans
always requires private mortgage insurance regardless of the down payment amount
is issued exclusively by federally chartered banks and savings institutions

explanations.a: A conventional loan is defined by its lack of government insurance or guarantee; it is originated by private lenders under private underwriting standards.
explanations.b: VA-guaranteed loans are government-backed, making them non-conventional by definition.
explanations.c: PMI is required on conventional loans only when the LTV exceeds 80%; with a 20% or greater down payment, no PMI is needed.
explanations.d: Conventional loans are made by a wide variety of lenders, not exclusively federally chartered institutions.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: When a seller agrees to finance the buyer's purchase directly, accepting a mortgage or deed of trust instead of cash at closing, this arrangement is called:

answers.text: a land patent conveyance
a deed in lieu of foreclosure
an assumption of the seller's existing mortgage
seller financing, or a purchase-money mortgage

explanations.a: A land patent is a government document conveying public land to a private party; it is not a seller-financing term.
explanations.b: A deed in lieu of foreclosure is given by a defaulting borrower to a lender to avoid foreclosure; it is not a form of seller financing.
explanations.c: Assuming an existing mortgage means taking over the seller's loan with the original lender; seller financing involves the seller acting as the new lender.
explanations.d: When the seller extends credit to the buyer and takes back a mortgage or trust deed, the arrangement is seller financing, and the resulting lien is a purchase-money mortgage.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: Under a land contract (also called a contract for deed or installment sale contract), the buyer:

answers.text: receives the deed from the seller at the time the contract is signed and records it immediately
makes installment payments to the seller, who retains legal title until the contract is paid in full
receives the same legal rights as a fee simple owner from the first day of possession
automatically obtains an undivided interest in the seller's other properties as additional collateral

explanations.a: In a land contract, the deed is not delivered until the buyer has completed the agreed payments; the seller retains title in the meantime.
explanations.b: The land contract structure has the buyer making installments toward the purchase price while the seller holds legal title as security until the full price is paid.
explanations.c: The buyer holds equitable title — the right to obtain ownership upon completion of payments — but not legal title.
explanations.d: A land contract is limited to the subject property; it does not encumber the seller's unrelated real estate.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: In a real estate loan transaction, the promissory note is BEST described as:

answers.text: the document that transfers ownership of the property from seller to buyer
the lender's written commitment to fund the loan by a specified closing date
the borrower's written and signed promise to repay the debt
the insurance policy protecting the lender against title defects

explanations.a: A deed transfers ownership; the promissory note is a debt instrument, not a conveyance document.
explanations.b: A lender's commitment letter is the document committing to fund; the promissory note is the borrower's promise to repay.
explanations.c: A promissory note is a negotiable instrument in which the borrower personally promises to repay the stated sum under the specified terms.
explanations.d: Title insurance protects against title defects; the promissory note is the evidence of the debt obligation.

questions.name: Finance
questions.keyword: deed of trust trustee holds title
questions.text: A deed of trust differs from a traditional two-party mortgage in that a deed of trust involves three parties: the borrower (trustor), the lender (beneficiary), and a:

answers.text: neutral third-party trustee who holds legal title during the loan term as security
government guarantor who insures the loan against borrower default
co-signer who shares equal responsibility for making loan payments
title insurance company that guarantees the lender's security interest

explanations.a: In a deed of trust, the borrower conveys legal title to a trustee, who holds it on behalf of the lender until the loan is repaid or foreclosed.
explanations.b: A government guarantor is involved in FHA and VA loans, not in the deed of trust structure itself.
explanations.c: A co-signer is a party to the promissory note, not a structural component of the deed of trust.
explanations.d: The title insurance company does not hold title; the trustee does.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A judicial foreclosure differs from a non-judicial (power of sale) foreclosure in that a judicial foreclosure:

answers.text: proceeds faster than a non-judicial foreclosure because attorneys are not required
allows the lender to take possession immediately upon the first missed payment
applies only to commercial properties, not residential mortgages
requires the lender to file suit and obtain a court judgment before the property may be sold

explanations.a: Judicial foreclosure is typically slower, not faster, because it requires a court proceeding.
explanations.b: Neither judicial nor non-judicial foreclosure allows immediate possession on the first missed payment; a default period and notice are required.
explanations.c: Judicial foreclosure is available for both residential and commercial mortgages depending on state law.
explanations.d: The defining characteristic of judicial foreclosure is that the lender must sue the borrower, and the court must issue a judgment before the property is auctioned.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: After a foreclosure sale, the proceeds are insufficient to satisfy the full outstanding loan balance. In states that permit it, the lender may then seek a:

answers.text: deed in lieu of the remaining unpaid balance from the borrower
deficiency judgment against the borrower for the shortfall
second foreclosure action against the borrower's unrelated personal property
federal subsidy payment to cover the gap between the sale proceeds and the loan balance

explanations.a: A deed in lieu is a pre-foreclosure agreement in which the borrower voluntarily conveys the property; it is not a post-foreclosure collection remedy.
explanations.b: A deficiency judgment is a personal judgment against the borrower for the difference between what the foreclosure sale produced and the total debt owed.
explanations.c: A second foreclosure is not a recognized remedy for a post-sale deficiency; the lender pursues a personal judgment against the borrower.
explanations.d: No federal subsidy is automatically available to make lenders whole after a foreclosure shortfall.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: The Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act (RESPA) was enacted primarily to:

answers.text: set the maximum interest rate that lenders may charge on residential mortgage loans
require all residential sellers to use a licensed real estate agent
protect consumers by requiring disclosure of settlement costs and prohibiting kickbacks among settlement service providers
establish federal minimum down payment requirements on all residential mortgages

explanations.a: RESPA does not set interest rate caps; the Truth-in-Lending Act addresses rate disclosures.
explanations.b: There is no federal law requiring sellers to use an agent; RESPA governs settlement services, not representation requirements.
explanations.c: RESPA requires clear disclosure of closing costs (via the Loan Estimate and Closing Disclosure) and prohibits kickbacks and referral fees between settlement service providers.
explanations.d: Down payment requirements are set by loan programs and lenders; RESPA addresses settlement procedures, not down payments.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: RESPA Section 8 specifically prohibits which of the following practices?

answers.text: giving or accepting any fee, kickback, or thing of value for the referral of settlement service business
charging more than two discount points on any federally related mortgage loan
lenders using adjustable-rate products without providing a consumer handbook
brokers representing both buyer and seller in any federally related transaction

explanations.a: RESPA Section 8 bans kickbacks and unearned fees exchanged among settlement service providers — such as referral payments between lenders and real estate agents — because they inflate consumer costs.
explanations.b: RESPA does not set a cap on discount points; that is a lender pricing matter.
explanations.c: ARM consumer handbooks are required under Regulation Z, not RESPA Section 8.
explanations.d: Dual agency is a state license law matter; RESPA Section 8 addresses payment arrangements among settlement service providers.

questions.name: Finance
questions.keyword: APR reflects true cost of credit
questions.text: Under the Truth-in-Lending Act (Regulation Z), lenders must disclose the Annual Percentage Rate (APR) because the APR:

answers.text: establishes the maximum interest rate the lender may charge on the loan
determines the exact amount of the borrower's monthly principal and interest payment
represents the lender's own cost of funds on the secondary market
reflects the true cost of credit by incorporating the interest rate and certain fees into a single annual rate

explanations.a: The APR is a disclosure tool, not a rate ceiling; it does not cap what the lender may charge.
explanations.b: The monthly payment is calculated from the contract interest rate and loan amount, not the APR.
explanations.c: The lender's cost of funds is not the APR; the APR reflects the borrower's total financing cost.
explanations.d: The APR combines the stated interest rate with the effect of points, fees, and other financing charges to give consumers a standardized cost-of-credit comparison figure.

questions.name: Finance
questions.keyword: right of rescission three business days
questions.text: Under Regulation Z, when a borrower refinances her primary residence with a new lender, she has the right to cancel the transaction without penalty within:

answers.text: 30 days of receiving the final Closing Disclosure
three business days of consummation of the transaction
one business day of signing the loan application
seven calendar days of receiving the Loan Estimate

explanations.a: The rescission window is three business days after consummation, not 30 days after the Closing Disclosure.
explanations.b: Regulation Z grants a three-business-day right of rescission for refinances and home equity loans secured by the borrower's principal dwelling, running from the date of consummation.
explanations.c: The right of rescission begins at consummation, not at application.
explanations.d: Seven calendar days is the waiting period between issuance of the Loan Estimate and closing, not the rescission period.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: Real estate brokers in a market who agree among themselves to charge the same standard commission rate are MOST likely violating:

answers.text: RESPA, because agreed-upon rates constitute a form of unearned fee
Regulation Z, because commission agreements affect the disclosed APR
federal antitrust law by engaging in price-fixing
the Equal Credit Opportunity Act, which governs how lenders set fees

explanations.a: RESPA Section 8 prohibits kickbacks; it does not govern commission-rate agreements among competing brokers.
explanations.b: Regulation Z addresses lender cost-of-credit disclosures; it does not apply to brokerage commission agreements.
explanations.c: Agreement among competitors to fix prices — including real estate commission rates — is horizontal price-fixing, a per se violation of the Sherman Antitrust Act.
explanations.d: ECOA addresses credit discrimination; it does not apply to brokerage commission-rate agreements.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A buyer overstates her income on a mortgage application so that the lender approves a loan larger than she would otherwise qualify for. This conduct is BEST described as:

answers.text: mortgage fraud, which may constitute a federal criminal offense
a breach of the seller's disclosure duty owed to the lender
a RESPA violation requiring mandatory disclosure to the title company
a minor application error that mortgage lenders routinely waive

explanations.a: Intentional misrepresentation on a federally related mortgage application constitutes mortgage fraud, a federal crime under 18 U.S.C. § 1014, among other statutes.
explanations.b: The seller has no disclosure duty to the buyer's lender regarding the buyer's stated income.
explanations.c: RESPA Section 8 addresses kickbacks; intentional misrepresentation on a loan application is not a RESPA matter.
explanations.d: Overstating income is not a minor error; it is intentional misrepresentation and a serious federal offense.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: The Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) prohibits lenders from discriminating in the granting of credit on the basis of:

answers.text: the property's assessed value relative to its loan amount
the property's location within a particular school district
the loan officer's personal assessment of current market conditions
race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age, or receipt of public assistance

explanations.a: LTV ratios are standard underwriting criteria, not ECOA-protected characteristics.
explanations.b: Property location may affect underwriting but is not the basis of ECOA's protected classes, though redlining under fair lending laws is also prohibited.
explanations.c: A loan officer's market opinion is not an ECOA-protected characteristic.
explanations.d: ECOA prohibits credit discrimination based on race, color, religion, national origin, sex, marital status, age (provided the applicant is old enough to contract), or the fact that income derives from a public assistance program.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A mortgage lender calculates a borrower's debt-to-income (DTI) ratio by dividing:

answers.text: the property's appraised value by the borrower's gross annual income
the borrower's total recurring monthly debt obligations by gross monthly income
the requested loan amount by the borrower's total net worth
total annual housing costs by the borrower's federal income tax liability

explanations.a: Dividing value by income is not the DTI calculation; that would produce an affordability ratio, not a debt ratio.
explanations.b: DTI = total monthly debt payments (housing plus all other recurring debts) ÷ gross monthly income, expressed as a percentage.
explanations.c: Net worth includes assets, which are not part of the DTI calculation.
explanations.d: Tax liability is not used to calculate DTI; gross income is the denominator.

questions.name: Finance
questions.text: A mortgage broker differs from a mortgage lender in that a mortgage broker:

answers.text: funds mortgage loans directly from the firm's own capital reserves
approves loan applications on behalf of the federal government
acts as an intermediary who arranges loans between borrowers and lenders without using its own funds
is the same as a mortgage servicer that collects and processes monthly loan payments

explanations.a: A lender (not a broker) funds loans from its own capital; the broker earns a fee for arranging the transaction.
explanations.b: FHA-approved lenders may process government-insured loans, but mortgage brokers do not approve applications on behalf of the federal government.
explanations.c: A mortgage broker serves as a middleman, matching borrowers with lenders and facilitating the origination process without advancing its own funds.
explanations.d: A mortgage servicer manages ongoing payment collection after the loan is made; a mortgage broker is involved only in origination.
